summary: `wasi-http`: Request with long url before query parameter crashes host
description:
### Summary

A guest sending a request with `?` occurring after byte 65535 in the url string can cause a panic in the host. This occurs because wasmtime-wasi-http's dependency on `http` was at a low enough bound to encounter [`http` issue 855](https://github.com/hyperium/http/issues/855): the byte index of `?` is stored as a `u16` which can overflow. If indexing at the wrapped value results in an invalid character offset then the `http` crate will panic when trying to split at that offset. The fix to this issue is to require a more recent `http` crate version which includes the fix.

Guests can use the WASI http `set-path-with-query` to a string of any length and `wasmtime-wasi-http` will pass it unmodified to the `http` crate, so this is a guest-controlled panic in the host. It affects versions of wasmtime >= 46 with the WASIp3 interface and >= 48 with the WASIp2 interface. Earlier versions aren't affected because the panic in `http` happen in a thread and wasn't re-raised in the host.

### Patches

Patches are present in main and in 48.0.6 and 49.0.3.

### Workarounds

No known workarounds.
